confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from two web searches. One returned the RBA rate for 18 Nov 2026; the other returned price indexes from MyLifeElsewhere and Traveltables. Those indexes are crowd-sourced, and part of the Traveltables data dates from 2023. I adjusted the figures upward for inflation and for pricing in July 2026, which is the dry and peak tourist season. The two sources disagree widely on beer. I used a pint price near the higher MyLifeElsewhere figure of about A$10.50, because that matches typical Queensland pub pricing. I did not search directly for cocktail or wine prices. I estimated them from their usual Australian price relationship to beer (cocktail about 2x beer, glass of wine about 1.2x beer), so they are less certain. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates for peak season; I did not check any booking sites or listings. The exchange rate in the source figures is close to the RBA rate used here.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are based on regional Queensland tourist centres. The searched indexes put Cairns slightly cheaper than Canberra overall and cheaper than Sydney or Melbourne, but July demand for reef tourism pushes accommodation up.
